So you might find AIs more helpful in introductory courses than you do in 400-level and above courses.

units.why: 'It is the responsibility of the tool user to review the accuracy and ownership of any AI-generated content' puts a duty on the user to verify output, so P31 must; it also names ownership, hence the fit_note. It does not require AI use, so unit_stance neutral. P29 (own submitted work) does not fit.
units.fit_note: Also makes the user responsible for checking ownership (copyright) of AI output, not only accuracy. Also requires review of ownership (copyright) of AI-generated content, not only accuracy.

units.passage: Users are expected to apply critical judgment and appropriate validation when using AI outputs in academic, research, or operational contexts.
units.why: 'Users are expected to apply critical judgment and appropriate validation when using AI outputs' tells users what to do as they work with AI output, so phase during-work, modality should (an expectation), and P31 because it is about verifying output.

units.passage: Your success in this class depends entirely on the human validation step—adding your own unique expertise and critical thinking to the machine’s output.
units.why: 'Your success in this class depends entirely on the human validation step' expects students to check AI output, so P31, should.

units.passage: Verify AI-generated information using authoritative sources.
units.why: Core principle 'Assume outputs can be wrong. Verify AI-generated information using authoritative sources'; P31.

units.passage: AI tools can generate incorrect, fabricated or misleading content
units.why: States AI 'can generate incorrect, fabricated or misleading content ("hallucinations"), including citations, calculations and code behavior'; P31.
